notes: BYLAW NOT FOUND. Animal control services for the Village of Newbury are contracted to the Humane Society London & Middlesex (HSLM), which enforces Animal Control By-law Number 131-15. However, the full text of the bylaw is not available online.

collar_tag_req: Every owner of a dog in the Municipality, shall cause a dog tag to be securely affixed on the dog at all times and no person shall remove the tag from a licensed dog; however, a dog tag may be removed while a dog is being lawfully used for hunting in the bush.
dog_limit: A maximum of three (3) dogs is generally permitted before the premises is defined as a kennel (which requires a kennel licence).
notes: URL: https://www.northperth.ca/media/k1ul1lrb/65-2014-animal-control-by-law.pdf. While the Animal Control By-law lacks explicit LGD provisions, the Township's Noise Control By-law (32-AD-2001) is farm-friendly as it explicitly exempts 'Persistent barking, calling or whining or other similar persistent noise made by any domestic pet or animal kept or used for any purpose other than agriculture.'

bylaw_name: Animal Care and Control By-law No. 2003-077
collar_tag_req: Every owner of a dog shall: keep the dog identification tag, issued by the City as part of the registration, securely affixed on the collar or harness on the dog at all times.
dog_limit: Only three (3) dogs over twenty (20) weeks of age may be kept in a residence unless the premises is a licensed kennel, an accredited veterinary facility or a registered facility for temporary foster care.
notes: URL: https://ottawa.ca/en/living-ottawa/laws-licences-and-permits/laws/laws-z/animal-care-and-control-law-no-2003-077. The City's website explicitly states: 'Whether you reside in urban or rural Ottawa, dogs and cats are subject to the same animal control bylaws including pet registration and noise complaints from barking dogs.' There are no exemptions for farm dogs, LGDs, or rural properties for the 3-dog limit or licensing.

bylaw_name: Municipal Code Chapter 284 (Dog Licensing) & Chapter 285 (Care of Animals)
collar_tag_req: All dog owners in Orillia must license their dog(s). Failing to keep a dog tag securely affixed to a dog is an offence.
dog_limit: A maximum of two dogs is permitted per dwelling unit.
notes: URL: https://www.orillia.ca/en/living-here/animalcontrollicensing.aspx. An entirely urban-focused set of animal control codes with a strict 2-dog limit per household and a strict restriction against howling or barking excessively that is explicitly enforced '24 hours per day'. No working dog provisions found.

collar_tag_req: All cats, dogs and ferrets must have a licence in Oshawa. Lifetime licences require a microchip.
dog_limit: No person shall keep more than three dogs in and about any dwelling unit within the City.
notes: URL: https://www.oshawa.ca/media/0hxhuv13/responsiblepetowners14-2010.pdf. Standard urban 'Responsible Pet Owners By-law' with strict tethering and penning provisions. No definitions or exemptions for working farm dogs or LGDs.

collar_tag_req: Owners must obtain or renew dog licences.
dog_limit: Not explicitly stated in the Animal Control By-law, however, properties keeping dogs must comply with Kennel definitions and limits in the Comprehensive Zoning By-law.
notes: URL: https://www.pelham.ca/media/ao4j45pd/69-2024-animal-control-by-law.pdf. A newly enacted by-law that repeals all older animal control and dog licensing by-laws. While the Animal Control By-law itself does not explicitly define LGDs, the Town's Noise By-law (4454-2022) is farm-friendly as it explicitly exempts from nuisance noise: 'Persistent barking, howling, whining, squawking or other like sounds made by any Animal kept or used for any purpose other than a Normal Farm Practice carried on by an Agricultural Operation.'

collar_tag_req: Upon payment of the licence fee, the owner shall be provided with a tag and such tag shall be securely fixed on the animal to which it was issued at all times.
dog_limit: The Responsible Pet Ownership By-law states that you may own a maximum of 3 dogs per household.
notes: URL: https://www.pickering.ca/media/dfplhxaj/responsiblepetbylaw-acc.pdf. A standard urban Responsible Pet Ownership bylaw. Pickering actively investigates and fines nuisance barking dogs with no explicit exemption for agricultural noise found in the by-law.

collar_tag_req: On payment of the fee or fees, the owner shall be furnished with a Dog Tag for each dog. This dog tag shall be kept securely affixed to the dog at all times.
dog_limit: No more than two (2) dogs over the age of 16 weeks (4 months) may be kept in or about a dwelling unit or premises within the corporate limits of the Township of Perth East. This section shall not apply to any person who is entitled to and has obtained a Kennel License.
notes: URL: https://www.pertheast.ca/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/09_2017G.pdf. Standard animal control bylaw with a strict 2-dog limit. Properties with more than two dogs must obtain a kennel licence, which are only permitted within Agricultural zones, but there are no specific exemptions listed for unkennelled LGDs.

collar_tag_req: Every person shall procure a licence and have the dog registered. This dog tag shall be kept securely affixed to the dog at all times.
dog_limit: No person, except a person to whom a kennel licence has been issued, shall at any one time in any one location within the Corporation keep or harbor more than 3 dogs of an age in excess of 3 months.
notes: URL: https://puslinch.ca/wp-content/uploads/2019/09/Dog-Licence-By-Law.pdf. The Township of Puslinch requires anyone with more than 3 dogs to obtain a kennel license, which is strictly governed by proper zoning constraints. Although the Ontario Sheep Farmers (OSF) submitted a proposal to Puslinch Council in Jan 2023 to add LGD definitions and exemptions to their bylaw, the currently available materials do not reflect these changes.

collar_tag_req: Dogs tags must be securely fixed on the dog at all times until tag is renewed or replaced.
dog_limit: Limit of three dogs per property. Exemption: 'Any bonafide farmer who owns livestock... may harbour up to three dogs in addition to any licenced dogs for the property provided the predator protection does reside with the livestock they are protecting.'
notes: URL: https://www.ramara.ca/media/emlaswh0/2005_76caninecontrolbylaw.pdf. This bylaw is highly farm-friendly. It provides a specific 'Predator Protection' exemption that doubles the dog limit (+3 additional dogs) for bona fide farmers keeping dogs that reside with livestock.
